await $`git add -A tests`;
await commit(`Add golden cases: 2 s recordings, endfire, 6.9 kHz, multi-bin IFB

Three more single recordings (2500 Hz at 0°, 5800 Hz at 160°, 6900 Hz at
120°) and a multi-bin IFB case on the sum of the 300/1400/2500 Hz recordings
at 40°, generated with pyMUSIC (existing CSVs regenerate byte-for-byte). All
match pyMUSIC-with-eigh to < 4e-6 relative error.

The peak check against pyMUSIC-as-published now accepts the mirror image: the
line array's spectrum has equal peaks at θ and 360° − θ, and on the composite
rounding put pyMUSIC's argmax at 320° and ours at 40°.`);
await $`git push 2>&1`.text();
const newBody = body2.replace(`Independent of #8.`, `### Test-suite cleanup
- WAV/angle helpers shared through \`tests/common\` (noisy and broadband tests had their own copies), with an \`ErrorLog\` that lists every failing case and prints the worst error.
- Tolerances set from measured worst errors. Clean recordings land exactly on the true angle, so ±5° could hide a 4° regression: now 0.5° (one grid step) for clean data, 3° for the 90 frequency triples (worst 2.5°), 5°/5°/8° at 10/5/1 dB SNR (worst 3.0°/1.5°/5.0°).
- The nine-tone broadband test counted the 6900 Hz bin twice (9100 Hz aliases onto it); bins are now deduplicated.
- The noisy test walks files in sorted order, so its noise seeds no longer depend on directory order.

### More golden cases
- 2500 Hz at 0° (endfire, 2 s), 5800 Hz at 160° (2 s), 6900 Hz at 120°, and multi-bin IFB on a 300+1400+2500 Hz composite at 40°, generated with pyMUSIC. All match pyMUSIC-with-\`eigh\` to < 4e-6 relative error.
- The peak check against pyMUSIC-as-published accepts the mirror image θ ↔ 360° − θ (equal peaks on the line array).

Independent of #8.`);
await $`gh pr edit 9 --title ${'Fill test gaps, tighten tolerances; fix analytic_signal odd lengths and IFB overflow'} --body ${newBody}`.text();
await $`git status --short; git log --oneline main..`.text()

gh pr edit 9 --title 'Fill test gaps, tighten tolerances; fix analytic_signal odd lengths and IFB overflow' --body '## Summary
Fills test gaps found in a review of the suite, and fixes the two bugs those tests turned up.

### Bug fixes
- **`analytic_signal` on empty or odd-length input**: empty input panicked on `spectrum[0]`. For odd N, bin N/2 was treated as a Nyquist bin and left undoubled, so `Re(z)` no longer equalled the input. Now matches `scipy.signal.hilbert`; even-length input (all WAV fixtures) is unchanged.
- **`ifb_music_spectrum` overflow**: the per-bin spectra were multiplied before taking the root. With `bins = None` at `nfft = 1024`, the product of 512 spectra overflowed to `inf` on `single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s` (26 of 720 angles) and the argmax landed on one of them. The geometric mean is now a mean of logarithms.

### New tests (all fast)
- `hermitian_eigen` returns ascending eigenvalues (the old tests re-sorted before asserting) and satisfies `A·v = λ·v`; the noise subspace is orthogonal to the sources; too many sources panic.
- `steering_vector`: `+j2πfτ` convention below Nyquist, conjugate above, real within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist.
- `tests/synthetic_test.rs`: square and pentagon arrays with 1, 2 and 3 sources, built from the geometry rather than `steering_vector`. Flipping the steering sign makes all three DOA tests fail.
- IFB: finite with all bins, repeated bin equals single bin, out-of-range bins skipped, data shorter than a window is flat.
- `stft`: argument panics and overlapping-window start positions.

### Test-suite cleanup
- WAV/angle helpers shared through `tests/common` (noisy and broadband tests had their own copies), with an `ErrorLog` that lists every failing case and prints the worst error.
- Tolerances set from measured worst errors. Clean recordings land exactly on the true angle, so ±5° could hide a 4° regression: now 0.5° (one grid step) for clean data, 3° for the 90 frequency triples (worst 2.5°), 5°/5°/8° at 10/5/1 dB SNR (worst 3.0°/1.5°/5.0°).
- The nine-tone broadband test counted the 6900 Hz bin twice (9100 Hz aliases onto it); bins are now deduplicated.
- The noisy test walks files in sorted order, so its noise seeds no longer depend on directory order.

### More golden cases
- 2500 Hz at 0° (endfire, 2 s), 5800 Hz at 160° (2 s), 6900 Hz at 120°, and multi-bin IFB on a 300+1400+2500 Hz composite at 40°, generated with pyMUSIC. All match pyMUSIC-with-`eigh` to < 4e-6 relative error.
- The peak check against pyMUSIC-as-published accepts the mirror image θ ↔ 360° − θ (equal peaks on the line array).

Independent of #8.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -- --include-ignored`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)'

content.text:
I opened [PR #9](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/pull/9) from `feat/test-gaps` and pushed the remaining items onto it. It now has 8 commits, and I updated the PR description to match. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -- --include-ignored` all pass.

**The broadband results:** when every bin is used, the method itself gives poor results; it isn't a bug. IFB-MUSIC computes one MUSIC spectrum per frequency bin and averages them, with every bin counting equally. A single tone fills maybe 1–3 of the 512 bins at `nfft = 1024`. The other bins hold only noise and leakage, but MUSIC still treats their strongest direction as "the source". So hundreds of spectra pointing in arbitrary directions outvote a few correct ones, which is how a 40° source ended up at 281°. The usual remedies are to keep only bins with real energy (for example, a total power well above the median) or to weight each bin by its power. I can add either as an option to `ifb_music_spectrum`.

**What changed since the PR opened:**
- **Shared helpers:** the noisy and broadband tests now use `tests/common` instead of their own copies of the WAV reader and angle helpers. A new `ErrorLog` lists every failing case and prints the worst error per test, so tolerances can be checked with `cargo test -- --nocapture`. The noisy test now reads files in sorted order, so its random noise no longer depends on directory order.
- **Tighter tolerances:** every clean recording lands exactly on its true angle, so the old ±5° limit could hide a 4° regression. New limits, with the measured worst errors:

| Test | Worst error | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean recordings (narrowband, IFB, broadband) | 0.00° | ±5–10° | ±0.5° (one grid step) |
| Broadband frequency triples | 2.5° | ±5° | ±3° |
| Noise at 10 / 5 / 1 dB SNR | 3.0 / 1.5 / 5.0° | ±10 / 15 / 20° | ±5 / 5 / 8° |

  The noisy limits keep some headroom because their worst case depends on the random noise: at 10 dB it came out worse than at 5 dB. CLAUDE.md now describes these tolerances.
- **9100 Hz bin:** the nine-tone test no longer counts the 6900 Hz bin twice (9100 Hz aliases onto it).
- **More golden cases:** I generated these with the original pyMUSIC using `tests/golden/generate_golden.py`. They cover a 2 s recording at 0° (endfire), one at 160°, 6.9 kHz, and a three-tone composite using three IFB bins. All match pyMUSIC (with its Hermitian solver `eigh`) to within 4e-6 relative error. The existing golden files came out byte-for-byte identical.
- **Golden peak check:** the comparison with pyMUSIC as published now accepts the mirror-image angle. On the composite, pyMUSIC's peak was at 320° and ours at 40°. The two peaks are equally high on the line array, so which one wins comes down to rounding.

I didn't add golden cases at or above Nyquist (8 kHz). musicrs deliberately handles those differently from pyMUSIC, so the values would differ.

Should I add energy-based bin selection for broadband next? Note that PR #8 and PR #9 both edit `src/music.rs`, so whichever merges second may need a small rebase.

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**musicrs** is a Rust port of the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone/antenna arrays. Based on R. O. Schmidt's 1986 algorithm and the Python pyMUSIC implementation.

## Commands

```bash
# Build
cargo build
cargo build --release

# Test
cargo test              # all tests except slow ones (#[ignore = "slow"])
cargo test -- --include-ignored   # full suite, including slow tests (CI runs this)
cargo test --lib        # unit tests only
cargo test --test '*'   # integration tests only
cargo test --test golden_test   # parity with the original pyMUSIC spectra
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   # CI runs this and `cargo fmt --check`

# Documentation
cargo doc --open
```

## Architecture

```
src/
├── lib.rs      # Public API exports and crate-level docs
├── music.rs    # Core MUSIC algorithm (MusicEstimator, spectrum, DOA estimation)
└── stft.rs     # Signal processing (STFT, analytic signal via Hilbert transform)
tests/
├── common/mod.rs                # Shared WAV/filename/angle helpers
├── integration_test.rs          # Narrowband DOA on every WAV recording (±5°)
├── ifb_test.rs                  # IFB-MUSIC on the tone's bin (nfft 160), below Nyquist (±5°)
├── golden_test.rs               # Spectra vs. original pyMUSIC output in tests/golden/
├── broadband_test.rs            # IFB-MUSIC on composite multi-tone signals
├── noisy_data_test.rs           # Narrowband DOA with added white noise
├── golden/                      # pyMUSIC reference CSVs + generate_golden.py
└── data/single-source/*.wav     # 4-channel 24-bit 16kHz test recordings
```

**Key types:**
- `MusicEstimator` — main struct; configure antenna positions, angle search range/step, sample rate, and number of sources
- `MusicEstimator::estimate_doa_from_real()` — real-data entry point (analytic signal per channel, then `estimate_doa`), like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`
- `MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum()` — wideband variant; bin frequencies use the estimator's `sample_rate`, so tones above Nyquist cannot be recovered
- `analytic_signal()` — converts real signal to complex via Hilbert transform (FFT-based)
- `stft()` — Short-Time Fourier Transform with configurable window and overlap

**Core algorithm flow:**
1. Compute covariance matrix of complex multichannel input
2. Hermitian eigendecomposition (`faer`) → signal/noise subspace split
3. Compute MUSIC pseudo-spectrum using steering vectors
4. Peak detection → DOA estimates in radians

## Dependencies

| Crate | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `nalgebra` | Matrix types and linear algebra |

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**musicrs** is a Rust port of the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone/antenna arrays. Based on R. O. Schmidt's 1986 algorithm and the Python pyMUSIC implementation.

## Commands

```bash
# Build
cargo build
cargo build --release

# Test
cargo test              # all tests except slow ones (#[ignore = "slow"])
cargo test -- --include-ignored   # full suite, including slow tests (CI runs this)
cargo test --lib        # unit tests only
cargo test --test '*'   # integration tests only
cargo test --test golden_test   # parity with the original pyMUSIC spectra
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   # CI runs this and `cargo fmt --check`

# Documentation
cargo doc --open
```

## Architecture

```
src/
├── lib.rs      # Public API exports and crate-level docs
├── music.rs    # Core MUSIC algorithm (MusicEstimator, spectrum, DOA estimation)
└── stft.rs     # Signal processing (STFT, analytic signal via Hilbert transform)
tests/
├── common/mod.rs                # Shared WAV/filename/angle helpers
├── integration_test.rs          # Narrowband DOA on every WAV recording (±5°)
├── ifb_test.rs                  # IFB-MUSIC on the tone's bin (nfft 160), below Nyquist (±5°)
├── golden_test.rs               # Spectra vs. original pyMUSIC output in tests/golden/
├── broadband_test.rs            # IFB-MUSIC on composite multi-tone signals
├── noisy_data_test.rs           # Narrowband DOA with added white noise
├── golden/                      # pyMUSIC reference CSVs + generate_golden.py
└── data/single-source/*.wav     # 4-channel 24-bit 16kHz test recordings
```

**Key types:**
- `MusicEstimator` — main struct; configure antenna positions, angle search range/step, sample rate, and number of sources
- `MusicEstimator::estimate_doa_from_real()` — real-data entry point (analytic signal per channel, then `estimate_doa`), like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`
- `MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum()` — wideband variant; bin frequencies use the estimator's `sample_rate`, so tones above Nyquist cannot be recovered
- `analytic_signal()` — converts real signal to complex via Hilbert transform (FFT-based)
- `stft()` — Short-Time Fourier Transform with configurable window and overlap

**Core algorithm flow:**
1. Compute covariance matrix of complex multichannel input
2. Hermitian eigendecomposition (`faer`) → signal/noise subspace split
3. Compute MUSIC pseudo-spectrum using steering vectors
4. Peak detection → DOA estimates in radians

## Dependencies

| Crate | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `nalgebra` | Matrix types and linear algebra |
| `num-complex` | Complex number arithmetic |
| `rustfft` | FFT for STFT and Hilbert transform |
| `faer` | Numerically stable Hermitian eigendecomposition |
| `hound` (dev) | Reading WAV test fixtures |
| `approx` (dev) | Floating-point approximate equality in tests |

## Testing

Integration tests load WAV files from `tests/data/single-source/` and verify DOA estimates within **±5°** of the known ground truth. File naming convention:

```
single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav
```

Test data covers:
- Frequencies: 300 Hz – 9.1 kHz (in ~1.1 kHz steps)
- Angles: 0°, 40°, 80°, 120°, 160°
- Durations: 1 s and 2 s
- Array: Kinect 4-mic geometry

## Workflow

- Before implementing a non-trivial change, propose a plan and get it approved first. While planning, ask clarifying questions about anything ambiguous (scope, API shape, defaults, test data) rather than guessing.

- Make changes on a branch, never directly on `main`:
  - `feat/<feature-name>` for new features
  - `fix/<bugfix-name>` for bug fixes
- Structure work in reasonably sized commits: each commit is one logical change that builds and passes tests on its own.
- A project Stop hook (`.claude/settings.json` → `.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`) runs `cargo test` when a turn ends with changed code under `src/`, `tests/` or `Cargo.*`, and sends failures back to Claude. Tests that take more than ~10 s are marked `#[ignore = "slow"]`, so the hook skips them; run `cargo test -- --include-ignored` for the full suite. Set `MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1` before starting Claude Code to turn the hook off.

## Notes

- Rust edition 2024, MSRV follows current stable toolchain
- No `rustfmt.toml` or `clippy.toml` — use `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` defaults
- Golden files: `*.eigh.csv` (pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eigh`) must match value-by-value; `*.eig.csv` (pyMUSIC as published) only by peak location, because `np.linalg.eig` returns a non-orthogonal noise basis on this near-noiseless data. Regenerate with the command in `tests/golden/generate_golden.py`.
- Sign convention: musicrs uses a non-conjugated analytic signal with an `exp(+j2πfτ)` steering vector; pyMUSIC conjugates the analytic signal and uses `exp(−j2πfτ)`. Equivalent below Nyquist. The above-Nyquist sign flip and the real steering vector at Nyquist are musicrs additions tuned to the test data.

"""Generate golden MUSIC spectra with the original pyMUSIC implementation.

Usage (from the repo root):

    git clone https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC /path/to/pyMUSIC
    git clone https://github.com/Trion/pySoundToolbox /path/to/pySoundToolbox
    uv run --python 3.10 --with 'numpy==1.23.5' python -I tests/golden/generate_golden.py \
        /path/to/pyMUSIC /path/to/pySoundToolbox

pyMUSIC was written against an old numpy/Python 2. numpy 1.23 still has the
`np.float` / `np.complex` aliases and still converts the 1x1 matrix in
`getSpectrum` to a scalar, so pyMUSIC.py runs unchanged. One shim remains:
  * pySoundToolbox.genAnalyticSignal uses `n / 2` as an index (Python 2
    integer division); it is re-executed with `n // 2`.
The algorithm itself is not modified.

Each case is computed twice:
  * `*.eig.csv`  – pyMUSIC exactly as published (`np.linalg.eig`).
  * `*.eigh.csv` – the same code with `np.linalg.eig` swapped for the Hermitian solver
    `np.linalg.eigh`. On this nearly noiseless data the noise eigenvalues are ~1e-15,
    and `eig` returns non-orthogonal noise eigenvectors, so the as-published spectrum
    depends on an arbitrary basis. Only its peak location is meaningful; musicrs
    (which uses a Hermitian solver) is compared value-by-value against `eigh`.

Output: CSVs in tests/golden/, columns `angle_rad,spectrum`.
"""

import os
import sys
import types
import wave

import numpy as np

pymusic_dir, toolbox_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

# Load genAnalyticSignal with the Python-2 index fix, exposed as pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox
with open(os.path.join(toolbox_dir, "pySoundToolbox.py")) as f:
    src = f.read()
start = src.index("def genAnalyticSignal")
end = src.index("\nclass ", start)
func_src = src[start:end].replace("n / 2", "n // 2")
toolbox_mod = types.ModuleType("pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox")
toolbox_mod.np = np
exec(func_src, toolbox_mod.__dict__)
pkg = types.ModuleType("pySoundToolbox")
pkg.pySoundToolbox = toolbox_mod
sys.modules["pySoundToolbox"] = pkg
sys.modules["pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox"] = toolbox_mod

sys.path.insert(0, pymusic_dir)
import pyMUSIC  # noqa: E402

DATA_DIR = "tests/data/single-source"
OUT_DIR = "tests/golden"
SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
NFFT = 160  # 100 Hz bins: every test tone falls exactly on a bin


def read_wav_4ch(path):
    """24-bit PCM, 4 channels -> (4, n) float array normalised by 2**23 (same as the Rust tests)."""
    with wave.open(path, "rb") as w:
        assert w.getnchannels() == 4 and w.getsampwidth() == 3
        raw = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.uint8)
    b = raw.reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.int32)
    v = b[:, 0] | (b[:, 1] << 8) | (b[:, 2] << 16)
    v = np.where(v & 0x800000, v - (1 << 24), v)
    return (v.reshape(-1, 4).T / 2.0**23).astype(np.float64)


def write_csv(name, spectrum, angles):
    with open(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name), "w") as f:
        f.write("angle_rad,spectrum\n")
        for a, s in zip(angles, spectrum):
            f.write(f"{float(a)!r},{float(s)!r}\n")


CASES = [
    ("single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s.wav", 300),
    ("single-source_1400Hz_40deg_1.0s.wav", 1400),
    ("single-source_4700Hz_120deg_1.0s.wav", 4700),
    ("single-source_2500Hz_0deg_2.0s.wav", 2500),
    ("single-source_5800Hz_160deg_2.0s.wav", 5800),
    ("single-source_6900Hz_120deg_1.0s.wav", 6900),
]

# Multi-bin IFB on the sum of several recordings at the same DOA (one bin per tone)
COMPOSITE_CASES = [
    ("composite_300+1400+2500Hz_40deg_2.0s", [300, 1400, 2500], 40, "2.0s"),
]

def run_case(fname, freq, solver):
    data = read_wav_4ch(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, fname))
    stem = fname[: -len(".wav")]
    est = pyMUSIC.MUSICEst()

    # Narrowband: same steps as MUSICEst.getSourceAngles, stopping before its (buggy) peak picking
    analytic = np.matrix(np.vstack([pyMUSIC.genAnalyticSignal(row) for row in data]).astype(np.complex128))
    cov = (analytic * analytic.H) / data.shape[1]
    noise_mat = est.getNoiseMat(cov, 1)
    spectrum, angles = est.getSpectrum(noise_mat, freq)
    write_csv(f"{stem}.narrowband.{solver}.csv", spectrum, angles)

    # IFB on the single bin holding the tone
    bin_idx = freq * NFFT // SAMPLE_RATE
    spectrum, angles = pyMUSIC.IFBMUSICSpectrum(data, est.antennaPositions, NFFT, bins=[bin_idx])
    write_csv(f"{stem}.ifb_nfft{NFFT}_bin{bin_idx}.{solver}.csv", spectrum, angles)
    print("wrote", stem, solver)


def run_composite(name, freqs, doa, duration, solver):
    parts = [read_wav_4ch(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, f"single-source_{f}Hz_{doa}deg_{duration}.wav")) for f in freqs]
    n = min(p.shape[1] for p in parts)
    data = sum(p[:, :n] for p in parts)
    bins = [f * NFFT // SAMPLE_RATE for f in freqs]
    est = pyMUSIC.MUSICEst()
    spectrum, angles = pyMUSIC.IFBMUSICSpectrum(data, est.antennaPositions, NFFT, bins=bins)
    write_csv(f"{name}.ifb_nfft{NFFT}_bins{'-'.join(map(str, bins))}.{solver}.csv", spectrum, angles)
    print("wrote", name, solver)

for solver, eig in [("eig", original_eig), ("eigh", np.linalg.eigh)]:

    for name, freqs, doa, duration in COMPOSITE_CASES:

np.linalg.eig = original_eig

// Parity with the original pyMUSIC implementation.
//
// The CSVs in tests/golden/ were produced by running pyMUSIC on the WAV test data
// (see tests/golden/generate_golden.py), in two variants:
//   * `*.eigh.csv` – pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eig` swapped for the Hermitian `eigh`.
//     musicrs must match these value-by-value.
//   * `*.eig.csv`  – pyMUSIC as published. On this nearly noiseless data `eig`
//     returns a non-orthogonal noise basis, so the values are basis-dependent; only
//     the peak location is compared.

mod common;

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

use musicrs::{MusicEstimator, analytic_signal};
use nalgebra::DMatrix;

const GOLDEN_DIR: &str = "./tests/golden";
const NFFT: usize = 160;
// Noise eigenvalues are ~1e-15 and pyMUSIC builds steering vectors in float128,
// so agreement is ~1e-7..1e-6 rather than machine precision.
const REL_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-4;

const CASES: [(&str, f64); 6] = [
    ("single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s", 300.0),
    ("single-source_1400Hz_40deg_1.0s", 1400.0),
    ("single-source_4700Hz_120deg_1.0s", 4700.0),
    ("single-source_2500Hz_0deg_2.0s", 2500.0),
    ("single-source_5800Hz_160deg_2.0s", 5800.0),
    ("single-source_6900Hz_120deg_1.0s", 6900.0),
];

fn read_golden(name: &str) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(Path::new(GOLDEN_DIR).join(name))
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("cannot read golden file {name}: {e}"));
    text.lines()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|line| {
            let (a, s) = line.split_once(',').unwrap();
            (a.parse::<f64>().unwrap(), s.parse::<f64>().unwrap())
        })
        .unzip()
}

fn argmax(v: &[f64]) -> usize {
    (0..v.len()).max_by(|&a, &b| v[a].total_cmp(&v[b])).unwrap()
}

/// Compare a musicrs spectrum against both golden variants of `prefix`.
fn check(prefix: &str, angles: &[f64], spectrum: &[f64]) {
    // Value-by-value against pyMUSIC with a Hermitian eigensolver
    let (g_angles, g_spectrum) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eigh.csv"));
    assert_eq!(angles.len(), g_angles.len(), "{prefix}: grid size differs");
    for (a, g) in angles.iter().zip(&g_angles) {
        assert!(
            (a - g).abs() < 1e-9,
            "{prefix}: angle grid differs ({a} vs {g})"
        );
    }
    let err = spectrum
        .iter()
        .zip(&g_spectrum)
        .map(|(s, g)| (s - g).abs() / g.abs())
        .fold(0.0, f64::max);
    println!("{prefix}: max relative error vs eigh {err:.3e}");
    assert!(
        err < REL_TOLERANCE,
        "{prefix}: deviates from pyMUSIC (eigh) by {err:.3e}"
    );

    // Peak location against pyMUSIC as published (within one grid step, circularly). The
    // line array's spectrum has equal peaks at θ and 360° − θ (grid index n − i), and
    // rounding decides which one is the argmax, so either counts.
    let (_, orig) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eig.csv"));
    let (ours, theirs) = (argmax(spectrum), argmax(&orig));
    let n = spectrum.len();
    let circular_steps = |a: usize, b: usize| {
        let d = (a + n - b) % n;
        d.min(n - d)
    };
    let steps = circular_steps(ours, theirs).min(circular_steps(ours, (n - theirs) % n));
    println!(
        "{prefix}: peak {:.1}° vs pyMUSIC (eig) {:.1}°",
        angles[ours].to_degrees(),
        angles[theirs].to_degrees()
    );
    assert!(
        steps <= 1,
        "{prefix}: peak differs from pyMUSIC (eig) by {steps} grid steps"
    );
}

#[test]
fn narrowband_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (stem, freq) in CASES {
        let (_, data) =
            common::read_wav_4ch(&Path::new(common::DATA_DIR).join(format!("{stem}.wav")));
        let analytic: Vec<Vec<_>> = (0..data.nrows())
            .map(|m| analytic_signal(&data.row(m).iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()))
            .collect();
        let x = DMatrix::from_fn(data.nrows(), data.ncols(), |m, t| analytic[m][t]);
        let cov = (&x * x.adjoint()).scale(1.0 / data.ncols() as f64);
        let noise = est.noise_subspace(&cov, 1);
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.spectrum(&noise, freq);
        check(&format!("{stem}.narrowband"), &angles, &spectrum);
    }
}

#[test]
fn ifb_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (stem, freq) in CASES {
        let (_, data) =
            common::read_wav_4ch(&Path::new(common::DATA_DIR).join(format!("{stem}.wav")));
        let bin = (freq * NFFT as f64 / est.sample_rate).round() as usize;
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[bin]));
        check(
            &format!("{stem}.ifb_nfft{NFFT}_bin{bin}"),
            &angles,
            &spectrum,
        );
    }
}

/// Multi-bin IFB (geometric mean over one bin per tone) on the sum of three recordings at 40°.
#[test]
fn ifb_multi_bin_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let freqs = [300, 1400, 2500];
    let parts: Vec<DMatrix<f64>> = freqs
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| common::read_wav_4ch(&common::wav_path(f, 40, "2.0s")).1)
        .collect();
    let n = parts.iter().map(|p| p.ncols()).min().unwrap();
    let data = parts
        .iter()
        .fold(DMatrix::zeros(4, n), |acc, p| acc + p.columns(0, n));
    let bins: Vec<usize> = freqs
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| f as usize * NFFT / est.sample_rate as usize)
        .collect();
    let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&bins));
    check(
        "composite_300+1400+2500Hz_40deg_2.0s.ifb_nfft160_bins3-14-25",
        &angles,
        &spectrum,
    );
}

DATA_DIR = "tests/data/single-source"

def read_wav_4ch(path):
    """24-bit PCM, 4 channels -> (4, n) float array normalised by 2**23 (same as the Rust tests)."""
    with wave.open(path, "rb") as w:
        assert w.getnchannels() == 4 and w.getsampwidth() == 3
        raw = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.uint8)
    b = raw.reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.int32)
    v = b[:, 0] | (b[:, 1] << 8) | (b[:, 2] << 16)
    v = np.where(v & 0x800000, v - (1 << 24), v)
    return (v.reshape(-1, 4).T / 2.0**23).astype(np.float64)


def write_csv(name, spectrum, angles):

def run_case(fname, freq, solver):

// Parity with the original pyMUSIC implementation.
//
// The CSVs in tests/golden/ were produced by running pyMUSIC on the WAV test data
// (see tests/golden/generate_golden.py), in two variants:
//   * `*.eigh.csv` – pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eig` swapped for the Hermitian `eigh`.
//     musicrs must match these value-by-value.
//   * `*.eig.csv`  – pyMUSIC as published. On this nearly noiseless data `eig`
//     returns a non-orthogonal noise basis, so the values are basis-dependent; only
//     the peak location is compared.

mod common;

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

use musicrs::{MusicEstimator, analytic_signal};
use nalgebra::DMatrix;

const GOLDEN_DIR: &str = "./tests/golden";
const NFFT: usize = 160;
// Noise eigenvalues are ~1e-15 and pyMUSIC builds steering vectors in float128,
// so agreement is ~1e-7..1e-6 rather than machine precision.
const REL_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-4;

const CASES: [(&str, f64); 6] = [
    ("single-source_300Hz_80deg_1.0s", 300.0),
    ("single-source_1400Hz_40deg_1.0s", 1400.0),
    ("single-source_4700Hz_120deg_1.0s", 4700.0),
    ("single-source_2500Hz_0deg_2.0s", 2500.0),
    ("single-source_5800Hz_160deg_2.0s", 5800.0),
    ("single-source_6900Hz_120deg_1.0s", 6900.0),
];

fn read_golden(name: &str) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(Path::new(GOLDEN_DIR).join(name))
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("cannot read golden file {name}: {e}"));
    text.lines()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|line| {
            let (a, s) = line.split_once(',').unwrap();
            (a.parse::<f64>().unwrap(), s.parse::<f64>().unwrap())
        })
        .unzip()
}

fn argmax(v: &[f64]) -> usize {
    (0..v.len()).max_by(|&a, &b| v[a].total_cmp(&v[b])).unwrap()
}

/// Compare a musicrs spectrum against both golden variants of `prefix`.
fn check(prefix: &str, angles: &[f64], spectrum: &[f64]) {
    // Value-by-value against pyMUSIC with a Hermitian eigensolver
    let (g_angles, g_spectrum) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eigh.csv"));
    assert_eq!(angles.len(), g_angles.len(), "{prefix}: grid size differs");
    for (a, g) in angles.iter().zip(&g_angles) {
        assert!(
            (a - g).abs() < 1e-9,
            "{prefix}: angle grid differs ({a} vs {g})"
        );
    }
    let err = spectrum
        .iter()
        .zip(&g_spectrum)
        .map(|(s, g)| (s - g).abs() / g.abs())
        .fold(0.0, f64::max);
    println!("{prefix}: max relative error vs eigh {err:.3e}");
    assert!(
        err < REL_TOLERANCE,
        "{prefix}: deviates from pyMUSIC (eigh) by {err:.3e}"
    );

    // Peak location against pyMUSIC as published (within one grid step, circularly). The
    // line array's spectrum has equal peaks at θ and 360° − θ (grid index n − i), and
    // rounding decides which one is the argmax, so either counts.
    let (_, orig) = read_golden(&format!("{prefix}.eig.csv"));
    let (ours, theirs) = (argmax(spectrum), argmax(&orig));
    let n = spectrum.len();
    let circular_steps = |a: usize, b: usize| {
        let d = (a + n - b) % n;
        d.min(n - d)
    };
    let steps = circular_steps(ours, theirs).min(circular_steps(ours, (n - theirs) % n));
    println!(
        "{prefix}: peak {:.1}° vs pyMUSIC (eig) {:.1}°",
        angles[ours].to_degrees(),
        angles[theirs].to_degrees()
    );
    assert!(
        steps <= 1,
        "{prefix}: peak differs from pyMUSIC (eig) by {steps} grid steps"
    );
}

#[test]
fn narrowband_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (stem, freq) in CASES {
        let (_, data) =
            common::read_wav_4ch(&Path::new(common::DATA_DIR).join(format!("{stem}.wav")));
        let analytic: Vec<Vec<_>> = (0..data.nrows())
            .map(|m| analytic_signal(&data.row(m).iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()))
            .collect();
        let x = DMatrix::from_fn(data.nrows(), data.ncols(), |m, t| analytic[m][t]);
        let cov = (&x * x.adjoint()).scale(1.0 / data.ncols() as f64);
        let noise = est.noise_subspace(&cov, 1);
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.spectrum(&noise, freq);
        check(&format!("{stem}.narrowband"), &angles, &spectrum);
    }
}

#[test]
fn ifb_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    for (stem, freq) in CASES {
        let (_, data) =
            common::read_wav_4ch(&Path::new(common::DATA_DIR).join(format!("{stem}.wav")));
        let bin = (freq * NFFT as f64 / est.sample_rate).round() as usize;
        let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&[bin]));
        check(
            &format!("{stem}.ifb_nfft{NFFT}_bin{bin}"),
            &angles,
            &spectrum,
        );
    }
}

/// Multi-bin IFB (geometric mean over one bin per tone) on the sum of three recordings at 40°.
#[test]
fn ifb_multi_bin_spectrum_matches_pymusic() {
    let est = MusicEstimator::default();
    let freqs = [300, 1400, 2500];
    let parts: Vec<DMatrix<f64>> = freqs
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| common::read_wav_4ch(&common::wav_path(f, 40, "2.0s")).1)
        .collect();
    let n = parts.iter().map(|p| p.ncols()).min().unwrap();
    let data = parts
        .iter()
        .fold(DMatrix::zeros(4, n), |acc, p| acc + p.columns(0, n));
    let bins: Vec<usize> = freqs
        .iter()
        .map(|&f| f as usize * NFFT / est.sample_rate as usize)
        .collect();
    let (spectrum, angles) = est.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, NFFT, 1, Some(&bins));
    check(
        "composite_300+1400+2500Hz_40deg_2.0s.ifb_nfft160_bins3-14-25",
        &angles,
        &spectrum,
    );
}

//! Helpers shared by the WAV-based integration tests.

#![allow(dead_code)]

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use nalgebra::DMatrix;

pub const DATA_DIR: &str = "./tests/data/single-source";

/// Ground truth encoded in a test-data filename.
pub struct Meta {
    pub frequency_hz: f64,
    pub doa_deg: f64,
    pub duration_s: f64,
}

/// Parse `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`.
pub fn parse_meta(path: &Path) -> Meta {
    let stem = path
        .file_stem()
        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
        .expect("bad file name");
    let parts: Vec<&str> = stem.split('_').collect();
    let num = |s: &str, suffix: &str| -> f64 { s.strip_suffix(suffix).unwrap().parse().unwrap() };
    Meta {
        frequency_hz: num(parts[1], "Hz"),
        doa_deg: num(parts[2], "deg"),
        duration_s: num(parts[3], "s"),
    }
}

/// Path of the recording at `freq_hz` / `doa_deg` / `duration` (e.g. `"2.0s"`).
pub fn wav_path(freq_hz: u32, doa_deg: u32, duration: &str) -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(DATA_DIR).join(format!(
        "single-source_{freq_hz}Hz_{doa_deg}deg_{duration}.wav"
    ))
}

/// All WAV files in the single-source data directory, sorted by name.
pub fn wav_files() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut paths: Vec<PathBuf> = fs::read_dir(DATA_DIR)
        .expect("Test data directory not found")
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().path())
        .filter(|p| p.extension().and_then(|ext| ext.to_str()) == Some("wav"))
        .collect();
    paths.sort();
    paths
}

/// Read a 4-channel, 24-bit PCM WAV file with `hound` and return
/// `(sample_rate, data)` where `data` is a `(4 × n_samples)` real matrix
/// normalised to `[-1, 1]`.
pub fn read_wav_4ch(path: &Path) -> (u32, DMatrix<f64>) {
    let mut reader = hound::WavReader::open(path).expect("Failed to open WAV file");
    let spec = reader.spec();
    assert_eq!(spec.channels, 4, "Expected 4-channel WAV");
    assert_eq!(spec.bits_per_sample, 24, "Expected 24-bit PCM");

    let raw_samples: Vec<i32> = reader
        .samples::<i32>()
        .map(|s| s.expect("Sample read error"))
        .collect();

    let n_channels = spec.channels as usize;
    let n_samples = raw_samples.len() / n_channels;
    let scale = 2.0_f64.powi(23); // 24-bit signed → [-1, 1]

    // De-interleave: WAV stores [ch0, ch1, ch2, ch3, ch0, ch1, ...]
    let mut data = DMatrix::<f64>::zeros(n_channels, n_samples);
    for (idx, &sample) in raw_samples.iter().enumerate() {
        data[(idx % n_channels, idx / n_channels)] = sample as f64 / scale;
    }

    (spec.sample_rate, data)
}

/// Smallest circular distance in degrees between `estimate_deg` and any of `truths_deg`.
pub fn angular_error(estimate_deg: f64, truths_deg: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    truths_deg
        .iter()
        .map(|&t| {
            let d = (estimate_deg - t).rem_euclid(360.0);
            d.min(360.0 - d)
        })
        .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min)
}

/// Angles indistinguishable from `doa_deg` for the Kinect line array (all mics on the
/// x axis): its mirror image `360° − θ`, plus `180° ± θ` at exactly Nyquist, where the
/// steering vector is real.
pub fn equivalent_angles(doa_deg: f64, frequency_hz: f64, sample_rate: f64) -> Vec<f64> {
    if (frequency_hz - sample_rate / 2.0).abs() < 0.5 {
        vec![doa_deg, 360.0 - doa_deg, 180.0 - doa_deg, 180.0 + doa_deg]
    } else {
        vec![doa_deg, 360.0 - doa_deg]
    }
}

/// Collects one angular error per case and checks them all at the end, so a failing run
/// lists every failing case, and a passing run prints the worst error (useful when tuning
/// tolerances).
pub struct ErrorLog {
    label: String,
    cases: Vec<(String, f64)>,
}

impl ErrorLog {
    pub fn new(label: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            label: label.into(),
            cases: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn record(&mut self, case: impl Into<String>, error_deg: f64) {
        self.cases.push((case.into(), error_deg));
    }

    /// Panics if there are no cases or any error exceeds `tolerance_deg`.
    pub fn check(&self, tolerance_deg: f64) {
        let label = &self.label;
        let (worst_case, worst) = self
            .cases
            .iter()
            .max_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label}: no cases ran"));
        println!(
            "{label}: {} cases, worst error {worst:.2}° ({worst_case}), tolerance ±{tolerance_deg}°",
            self.cases.len()
        );
        let failures: Vec<String> = self
            .cases
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, e)| *e > tolerance_deg)
            .map(|(c, e)| format!("  {c}: error {e:.2}°"))
            .collect();
        assert!(
            failures.is_empty(),
            "{label}: {}/{} cases exceed ±{tolerance_deg}°:\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            self.cases.len(),
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }
}

    }
}

/// Collects one angular error per case and checks them all at the end, so a failing run
/// lists every failing case, and a passing run prints the worst error (useful when tuning
/// tolerances).
pub struct ErrorLog {
    label: String,
    cases: Vec<(String, f64)>,
}

impl ErrorLog {
    pub fn new(label: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            label: label.into(),
            cases: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn record(&mut self, case: impl Into<String>, error_deg: f64) {
        self.cases.push((case.into(), error_deg));
    }

    /// Panics if there are no cases or any error exceeds `tolerance_deg`.
    pub fn check(&self, tolerance_deg: f64) {
        let label = &self.label;
        let (worst_case, worst) = self
            .cases
            .iter()
            .max_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label}: no cases ran"));
        println!(
            "{label}: {} cases, worst error {worst:.2}° ({worst_case}), tolerance ±{tolerance_deg}°",
            self.cases.len()
        );
        let failures: Vec<String> = self
            .cases
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, e)| *e > tolerance_deg)
            .map(|(c, e)| format!("  {c}: error {e:.2}°"))
            .collect();
        assert!(
            failures.is_empty(),
            "{label}: {}/{} cases exceed ±{tolerance_deg}°:\n{}",
            failures.len(),
            self.cases.len(),
            failures.join("\n")
        );
    }
}

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**musicrs** is a Rust port of the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone/antenna arrays. Based on R. O. Schmidt's 1986 algorithm and the Python pyMUSIC implementation.

## Commands

```bash
# Build
cargo build
cargo build --release

# Test
cargo test              # all tests except slow ones (#[ignore = "slow"])
cargo test -- --include-ignored   # full suite, including slow tests (CI runs this)
cargo test --lib        # unit tests only
cargo test --test '*'   # integration tests only
cargo test --test golden_test   # parity with the original pyMUSIC spectra
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   # CI runs this and `cargo fmt --check`

# Documentation
cargo doc --open
```

## Architecture

```
src/
├── lib.rs      # Public API exports and crate-level docs
├── music.rs    # Core MUSIC algorithm (MusicEstimator, spectrum, DOA estimation)
└── stft.rs     # Signal processing (STFT, analytic signal via Hilbert transform)
tests/
├── common/mod.rs                # Shared WAV/filename/angle helpers, ErrorLog
├── integration_test.rs          # Narrowband DOA on every WAV recording (±0.5°)
├── ifb_test.rs                  # IFB-MUSIC on the tone's bin (nfft 160), below Nyquist (±0.5°)
├── golden_test.rs               # Spectra vs. original pyMUSIC output in tests/golden/
├── broadband_test.rs            # IFB-MUSIC on composite multi-tone signals
├── noisy_data_test.rs           # Narrowband DOA with added white noise
├── synthetic_test.rs            # Synthetic plane waves: 2-D arrays, 2–3 sources, no mirror ambiguity
├── golden/                      # pyMUSIC reference CSVs + generate_golden.py
└── data/single-source/*.wav     # 4-channel 24-bit 16kHz test recordings
```

**Key types:**
- `MusicEstimator` — main struct; configure antenna positions, angle search range/step, sample rate, and number of sources
- `MusicEstimator::estimate_doa_from_real()` — real-data entry point (analytic signal per channel, then `estimate_doa`), like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`
- `MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum()` — wideband variant; bin frequencies use the estimator's `sample_rate`, so tones above Nyquist cannot be recovered
- `analytic_signal()` — converts real signal to complex via Hilbert transform (FFT-based)
- `stft()` — Short-Time Fourier Transform with configurable window and overlap

**Core algorithm flow:**
1. Compute covariance matrix of complex multichannel input
2. Hermitian eigendecomposition (`faer`) → signal/noise subspace split
3. Compute MUSIC pseudo-spectrum using steering vectors
4. Peak detection → DOA estimates in radians

## Dependencies

| Crate | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `nalgebra` | Matrix types and linear algebra |
| `num-complex` | Complex number arithmetic |
| `rustfft` | FFT for STFT and Hilbert transform |
| `faer` | Numerically stable Hermitian eigendecomposition |
| `hound` (dev) | Reading WAV test fixtures |
| `approx` (dev) | Floating-point approximate equality in tests |

## Testing

Integration tests load WAV files from `tests/data/single-source/` and compare DOA estimates with the ground truth in the file name. Clean recordings land exactly on the true angle, so their tolerance is one 0.5° grid step; noisy and broadband-triple tests use tolerances set a little above the measured worst error. `common::ErrorLog` prints the worst error per test (`cargo test -- --nocapture`), which is the number to re-check before changing a tolerance. File naming convention:

```
single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav
```

Test data covers:
- Frequencies: 300 Hz – 9.1 kHz (in ~1.1 kHz steps)
- Angles: 0°, 40°, 80°, 120°, 160°
- Durations: 1 s and 2 s
- Array: Kinect 4-mic geometry

## Workflow

- Make changes on a branch, never directly on `main`:
  - `feat/<feature-name>` for new features
  - `fix/<bugfix-name>` for bug fixes
- Structure work in reasonably sized commits: each commit is one logical change that builds and passes tests on its own.
- A project Stop hook (`.claude/settings.json` → `.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`) runs `cargo test` when a turn ends with changed code under `src/`, `tests/` or `Cargo.*`, and sends failures back to Claude. Tests that take more than ~10 s are marked `#[ignore = "slow"]`, so the hook skips them; run `cargo test -- --include-ignored` for the full suite. Set `MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1` before starting Claude Code to turn the hook off.

## Notes

- Rust edition 2024, MSRV follows current stable toolchain
- No `rustfmt.toml` or `clippy.toml` — use `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` defaults
- Golden files: `*.eigh.csv` (pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eigh`) must match value-by-value; `*.eig.csv` (pyMUSIC as published) only by peak location, because `np.linalg.eig` returns a non-orthogonal noise basis on this near-noiseless data. Regenerate with the command in `tests/golden/generate_golden.py`.
- Sign convention: musicrs uses a non-conjugated analytic signal with an `exp(+j2πfτ)` steering vector; pyMUSIC conjugates the analytic signal and uses `exp(−j2πfτ)`. Equivalent below Nyquist. The above-Nyquist sign flip and the real steering vector at Nyquist are musicrs additions tuned to the test data.

git commit -q -am 'Add select_bins_by_energy for IFB-MUSIC

IFB-MUSIC weights every bin equally, so with bins = None the noise-only bins
dominate the geometric mean (single recordings off by up to ~130°). The new
helper keeps bins whose cross-spectral power is within threshold_db of the
strongest bin; its result goes into the existing bins argument.

With a 20 dB threshold, every recording below Nyquist is exact at nfft 160
(tones on bins). Three-tone composites are within 2.0° at nfft 160 and 1024;
at 1024 the tones fall between bins and leakage bins are steered at their own
frequency, which is documented on the function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'

content.text:
I added the energy-based bin selection on `feat/ifb-energy-bins`. The subagent did both golden tasks on `feat/golden-cases`, and the plan-first rule is in CLAUDE.md on `feat/claude-md-plan-first`. All three branches are committed locally, nothing is pushed, and the full suite (slow tests included) passes on each.

**Plan-first rule** (`37971df`, branched from `main`): CLAUDE.md now says to propose a plan, get it approved, and ask clarifying questions while planning. I followed it for the other two tasks.

**Energy-based bin selection** (`85aa62e`, branched from `feat/test-gaps`):
- **What it is:** a new public function, `select_bins_by_energy(&data, nfft, threshold_db)`. It returns the bins whose power is within `threshold_db` of the strongest bin, never the DC bin, and you pass the result to the existing `bins` argument.
- **Results with a 20 dB threshold:** with `bins = None` the worst error was about 130°.
  - At `nfft = 160` every tone falls exactly on a bin, so all 70 recordings below Nyquist come out exact.
  - Three-tone composites come out within 2.0°, at both `nfft = 160` and `1024`.
- **Where it falls short of the plan:** I expected ±0.5° everywhere, and that doesn't hold when tones fall between bins (`nfft = 1024`). The neighbouring bins that pick up the tone are steered at their own frequency rather than the tone's, which shifts the angle, most near endfire. Even selecting only the single strongest bin, a lone tone can be off by 5.5° at 0° and 1.5° elsewhere. This is a general IFB limitation; the old hand-picked-bin tests simply never ran single recordings at that size. So the composite test allows ±2.5°, and the function's docs say to choose `nfft` so tones land on bins.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the threshold, DC exclusion, silent or too-short data and a negative threshold; a doctest; and the two WAV tests above. Each WAV test takes about 5 s in a debug build, under the slow-test limit.

**Golden cases (subagent):** I re-ran the full suite in its worktree and checked its two commits.
- **More pyMUSIC cases** (`64871f4`): all five angles at 3.6 kHz and 6.9 kHz, both durations, and a second composite (3600 + 4700 + 5800 Hz at 120°). The worst error against pyMUSIC is 4.9e-6, and the existing golden files regenerated byte-for-byte.
